intro: I work with small product teams and independent founders who need a thoughtful builder — someone who can move between interface design, application logic and the details that make a release feel finished.

services.title: Full-stack product development
services.description: End-to-end delivery for web products: interface implementation, application logic, API integration, testing and launch support. Best for a focused first release or a well-defined product slice.
services.bestFor: Teams with a clear product idea and a need for one accountable builder.

services.title: Frontend engineering & design systems
services.tagline: Interfaces that scale with the product
services.description: A focused frontend engagement: building reusable components, clarifying design tokens and giving a growing product a UI foundation that stays consistent as more people contribute.
services.bestFor: Products whose interface has outgrown its original CSS or component patterns.

services.title: APIs & backend systems
services.description: Design and implementation of Node.js services and data models with understandable APIs, solid validation, sensible error states and a practical testing baseline.
services.bestFor: Teams adding a service layer or untangling an API that has become hard to change.

services.title: Performance, accessibility & SEO audits
services.tagline: Find the friction, fix what matters
services.description: A practical review of the things users and search engines feel: loading performance, core interactions, keyboard access, semantics and metadata. You get prioritised findings and implementation guidance.
services.bestFor: Teams that know something feels slow or difficult to use, but need a clear place to start.

process.title: Discover
process.description: Clarify the goal, the constraints and the people the product is for. We agree on what success looks like before building.

process.title: Define
process.description: Map the core flows, content and system boundaries. I turn the brief into a scoped plan with visible assumptions.

process.title: Build
process.description: Work in small, reviewable slices with working previews. Quality checks happen alongside the build, not after it.

process.title: Launch & refine
process.description: Ship with the right documentation and a short feedback loop. We fix what the real world reveals.

engagements.title: Project sprint
engagements.description: A defined scope delivered over a short, focused engagement. Good for a launch, a new feature or a product concept that needs to become real.

engagements.title: Embedded support
engagements.description: Ongoing collaboration with your existing team, with a regular cadence and a clear area of ownership. Good for products that are already moving.

engagements.title: Audit & roadmap
engagements.description: A structured review followed by a prioritised plan your team can execute, with optional follow-up support.

faqs.question: What kinds of projects are a good fit?
faqs.answer: Product teams that need a full-stack builder who cares about design quality, accessibility and maintainability. Web applications, internal tools, marketing sites with custom interactions and focused product experiments are all a good fit.

faqs.question: Do you work with existing teams?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can join an existing workflow, work alongside designers and engineers, and adapt to the tools and conventions the team already uses. Clear ownership and regular communication matter more than a particular process.

faqs.question: How do you handle timelines?
faqs.answer: I scope work in small slices, communicate assumptions early and keep a visible sequence of deliverables. After a short discovery conversation, I can propose a realistic plan with milestones and checkpoints.

faqs.question: Can you work remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes. I work remotely with teams across time zones and am based in Pacific Time. I keep communication asynchronous by default and schedule working sessions when they are useful.

faqs.question: What happens after launch?
faqs.answer: You receive the implementation, setup notes and a handover. If you want ongoing support, we can agree on a follow-up window or a lighter maintenance arrangement.
